I'm from Earth, near the middle, though on Emmer's side. Meredith, linguist, is on the other side of the middle. And beyond her, toward the far end, is Kelburn, mathematician. There's a corresponding span of fertility.

76536-the-loss-of-the-swansea.title: _A Story Of The Florida Coast_
76536-the-loss-of-the-swansea.creator: W. L. Alden
76536-the-loss-of-the-swansea.description: A book by W. L. Alden. Once a man hired father to sail a new brig from Bristol round to Penzance, and we went with him. That was the one week when we did not live in Bristol, which I just mentioned. We enjoyed it very much and learned a good deal about square-rigged vessels while we were in the brig.

arxiv-2110-07517.title: Ultra-high-energy neutrino scattering in an anomalous U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) effective field theory
arxiv-2110-07517.creator: Chuan-Hung Chen, Cheng-Wei Chiang, Chun-Wei Su
arxiv-2110-07517.description: Abstract A unique characteristic of exponentially growing scattering amplitude arises in an anomalous Abelian effective field theory when an extremely light Dirac neutrino mass is introduced to break the symmetry. We show that the low energy effective Lagrangian can be made explicitly gauge invariant with the help of a nonlinear representation of the Goldstone or Stueckelberg field.

arxiv-2208-01739.title: Reconstructing Sparse Multiplex Networks with Application to Covert Networks Journal: Entropy
arxiv-2208-01739.creator: Jin-Zhu Yü, Mincheng Wu, Gisela Bichler, Felipe Aros-Vera, Jianxi Gao
arxiv-2208-01739.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jin-Zhu Yü, Mincheng Wu, Gisela Bichler, Felipe Aros-Vera, Jianxi Gao. Network structure provides critical information for understanding the dynamic behavior of networks. However, the complete structure of real-world networks is often unavailable, thus it is crucially important to develop approaches to infer a more complete structure of networks. In this paper, we integrate the configuration model for generating random networks into an Expectation-Maximization-Aggregation (EMA) framework to reconstruct the complete structure of multiplex networks.

arxiv-2502-00706.title: Model Provenance Testing for Large Language Models
arxiv-2502-00706.creator: Ivica Nikolić, Teodora Baluta, Prateek Saxena
arxiv-2502-00706.description: Abstract Large language models are increasingly customized through fine-tuning and other adaptations, creating challenges in enforcing licensing terms and managing downstream impacts such as protecting intellectual property or identifying vulnerabilities. We address this challenge by developing a framework for testing model provenance .

arxiv-2506-05972.title: Bridging Domain Gaps in Agricultural Image Analysis: A Comprehensive Review From Shallow Adaptation to Deep Learning
arxiv-2506-05972.creator: Xing Hu, Siyuan Chen, Xuming Huang, Qianqian Duan, LingKun Luo, Ruijiao Li, Huiliang Shang, Linhua Jiang, Jianping Yang, Hamid Reza Karimi, Dawei Zhang
arxiv-2506-05972.description: Abstract With the growing application of computer vision in agriculture, image analysis has become essential for tasks such as crop health monitoring and pest detection. However, significant domain shifts caused by environmental variations, different crop types, and diverse data acquisition methods hinder model generalization across regions, seasons, and complex agricultural settings.

arxiv-2507-05872.title: LDP 3 : An Extensible and Multi-Threaded Toolkit for Local Differential Privacy Protocols and Post-Processing Methods
arxiv-2507-05872.creator: Berkay Kemal Balioglu, Alireza Khodaie, M. Emre Gursoy
arxiv-2507-05872.description: Abstract Local differential privacy (LDP) has become a prominent notion for privacy-preserving data collection. While numerous LDP protocols and post-processing (PP) methods have been developed, selecting an optimal combination under different privacy budgets and datasets remains a challenge. Moreover, the lack of a comprehensive and extensible LDP benchmarking toolkit raises difficulties in evaluating new protocols and PP methods.

arxiv-2508-01747.title: Revealing a ribbon-like jet in OJ 287 with RadioAstron
arxiv-2508-01747.creator: E. Traianou, J. L. Gómez, I. Cho, A. Chael, A. Fuentes, I. Myserlis, M. Wielgus, G.-Y. Zhao, R. Lico, K. Moriyama, L. Dey, G. Bruni, R. Dahale, T. Toscano, L. I. Gurvits, M. M. Lisakov, Y. Y. Kovalev, A. P. Lobanov, A. B. Pushkarev, K. V. Sokolovsky
arxiv-2508-01747.description: Abstract We present space-based very long baseline interferometry observations of the BL Lac type object OJ 287 taken with RadioAstron at 22 GHz on April 25, 2016, in conjunction with a ground array comprising 27 radio telescopes. We detect ground-space fringes at projected baselines extending up to 4.

arxiv-2510-17329.title: The first positive position of a lattice random walk
arxiv-2510-17329.creator: Claude Godrèche, Jean-Marc Luck
arxiv-2510-17329.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Claude Godrèche, Jean-Marc Luck. The distribution of the first positive position reached by a random walker starting at the origin is central to the analysis of extremes and records in one-dimensional random walks. In this work, we present a detailed and self-contained analytical study of this distribution for symmetric finite-range lattice walks, whose steps are drawn from a distribution supported on finitely many integers.

pmc-11313046.title: New Insights into Involvement of Low Molecular Weight Proteins in Complex Defense Mechanisms in Higher Plants
pmc-11313046.creator: Magdalena Ruszczyńska, Hubert Sytykiewicz, Bartolome Sabater
pmc-11313046.description: Dynamic climate changes pose a significant challenge for plants to cope with numerous abiotic and biotic stressors of increasing intensity. Plants have evolved a variety of biochemical and molecular defense mechanisms involved in overcoming stressful conditions. Under environmental stress, plants generate elevated amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and, subsequently, modulate the activity of the antioxidative enzymes.

pmc-11393370.title: Management of Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis in Adults: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Dermatologists Within the Asia–Pacific Region
pmc-11393370.creator: Chia-Yu Chu, Yung Chan, Siriwan Wananukul, Hao Cheng, Nisha Suyien Chandran, Ramesh Bhat, Sang Wook Son, Han-Fang Liao, Sean Gardiner, Qi Qing Ng, See-Hwee Yeo, Sophie Bozhi Chen, Yoko Kataoka
pmc-11393370.description: IntroductionLimited evidence is available on real-world management of atopic dermatitis (AD) among Asian adults. This cross-sectional study aimed to assess current approaches in AD diagnosis and management in Asia.MethodsPractising dermatologists regularly treating patients with moderate-to-severe AD were recruited from eight Asia–Pacific territories, namely Mainland China, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand.

pmc-11440281.title: Development of a prognostic nomogram for advanced non-small cell lung cancer using clinical characteristics
pmc-11440281.creator: Haoyue Qin, Zhe Huang, Huan Yan, Lianxi Song, Liang Zeng, Qinqin Xu, Wenhuan Guo, Shaoding Lin, Wenjuan Jiang, Zhan Wang, Li Deng, Xing Zhang, Fan Tong, Ruiguang Zhang, Zhaoyi Liu, Lin Zhang, Xiaorong Dong, Nong Yang, Yongchang Zhang
pmc-11440281.description: SummaryThis retrospective study demonstrated that patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer who experienced any-grade or grade 1–2 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) with immune checkpoint inhibitor plus chemotherapy (ICI+Chemo) as first-line treatment regimen had significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS; p < 0.001) and overall survival (OS; p < 0.05) compared with patients without any irAE.

pmc-11485202.title: Characterization and Clinical Outcome of Philadelphia Chromosome–Positive AML in Thrombocytopenia-Absent Radius Syndrome
pmc-11485202.creator: Alejandro Villar-Prados, Arman Odabas, Joshua R. Menke, Kerry Kingham, Gabriel N. Mannis
pmc-11485202.description: ological malignancies.1 One BMFS that is rarely associated with leukemic transformation is the autosomal recessive thrombocytopenia-absent radius (TAR) syndrome.2-4 TAR is characterized by the aplasia or hypoplasia of radii at birth, presence of both thumbs, and hypomegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia that persists through life.3 TAR is caused by inherited biallelic variants affecting the RBM8A gene.

pmc-11604812.title: Schizophrenia Biomarkers: Blood Transcriptome Suggests Two Molecular Subtypes
pmc-11604812.creator: Herut Dor, Libi Hertzberg
pmc-11604812.description: Schizophrenia is a chronic illness that imposes a significant burden on patients, their families, and the health care system. While it has a substantial genetic component, its heterogeneous nature—both genetic and clinical—limits the ability to identify causal genes and mechanisms.

pmc-12505264.title: Characterizing 13C Spectral Assignments and Substituent Distributions of Hydroxypropylmethylcellulose Acetyl Succinate Using Dynamic Nuclear Polarization Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
pmc-12505264.creator: Ronan P. Cosquer, Arthur C. Pinon, Mária Šoltésová, Lucy E. Hawarden, Anuji Abraham, Mike Tobyn, Frédéric Blanc
pmc-12505264.description: Hydroxypropylmethylcellulose acetyl succinate (HPMC-AS) is the most widely used polymer in commercially available amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs), due to its ability to aid dissolution of poorly soluble drugs while impeding drug recrystallization. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a well-suited approach to provide structural information on amorphous solids and access intermolecular interactions in multicomponent materials such as ASDs.

pmc-12635693.title: Management of peritoneal metastases from colorectal cancer and small bowel adenocarcinoma in patients with inflammatory bowel disease
pmc-12635693.creator: Daniel Paramythiotis, Dimitrios Tsavdaris, Georgios Geropoulos, Dominick Alessandro Sacchet, Kyriakos Psarras
pmc-12635693.description: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have an increased risk of developing colorectal cancer, which may ultimately result in peritoneal metastases (PM). PM in patients with IBD is by nature difficult to treat due to the chronic inflammation and immunosuppression inherent in IBD.

pmc-13026562.title: Socioeconomic Interventions for WHO’s End TB Strategy Targets: Insights from SIR Modelling in Kazakhstan
pmc-13026562.creator: Temirlan Ukubayev, Berik Koichubekov, Marina Sorokina, Donatas Austys
pmc-13026562.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? This study addresses the persistent public health challenge of tuberculosis in Kazakhstan by modeling its transmission dynamics, directly relating to the global issue of tuberculosis as one of leading causes of death.

pmc-13087453.title: Integrating Tissue Proteomics and Urinary Analyses to Capture Dynamic Podocyte Injury
pmc-13087453.creator: Xhuliana Kajana, Gianluca Caridi, Andrea Angeletti
pmc-13087453.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). mportant insights into disease-specific patterns of podocyte protein expression. Notably, they report a marked reduction of slit diaphragm and cytoskeletal podocyte proteins in minimal change disease and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, whereas such reduction was not observed in MN; a finding they appropriately describe as surprising, supporting that the pathophysiology of podocyte injury in MN differs from that in minimal change disease and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

pmc-13118124.title: Risk-Adapted Selective Elective Nodal Irradiation in the Total Neoadjuvant Therapy Era for Rectal Cancer
pmc-13118124.creator: Seung-Gu Yeo, Min-Jeong Kim, Kwang Hwan Cho, Jina Yun, Dae Ro Lim, Jung Cheol Kuk
pmc-13118124.description: With the introduction of total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) in locally advanced rectal cancer treatment, multidisciplinary treatment options have become more diverse than before, and many challenges remain unresolved. A randomized clinical study in intermediate-risk locally advanced rectal cancer showed that neoadjuvant full-dose systemic chemotherapy with response-adapted omission of radiation therapy is non-inferior to concurrent chemoradiotherapy.

pmc-13120237.title: Migration of Plastic Additives and Non-Intentionally Added Substances from Packaging into Edible Oils and Beverages: A Combined GC–MS and Hydrolysis–Capillary Electrophoresis Approach
pmc-13120237.creator: Rodica Sturza, Veronica Dragancea, Aliona Ghendov-Mosanu, Ileana-Denisa Nistor, Diana-Carmen Mirila, Dmitri Lazacovici
pmc-13120237.description: The present study aimed to investigate the migration of potentially hazardous compounds from plastic food packaging into edible oils, bottled water and soft drinks available on the market in the Republic of Moldova. GC–MS screening was applied to identify plastic additives and unintentionally added substances (NIAS).

pmc-13546556.title: MNAT1 in gastrointestinal cancers: mechanistic insights and therapeutic strategies—a narrative review
pmc-13546556.creator: Yanhua Zhang, Aiqi Hu, Chun Wen, Xi Yang, Xiaopai Wang, Sanping Zheng

pmc-13590591.title: Identification of DNA methylation signatures of smoking in women and associations with cardiovascular disease mortality
pmc-13590591.creator: Dennis Khodasevich, Aladdin H. Shadyab, Adam X. Maihofer, Caroline M. Nievergelt, Robert Wallace, Lisa W. Martin, Anne K. Bozack, Rosemarie de la Rosa, Marcia L. Stefanick, Nora Franceschini, Andres Cardenas
pmc-13590591.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tobacco smoking is critical risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, with epigenetics implicated as a key biological mechanism. Smoking disproportionately impacts CVD risk in women; however, limited research has examined smoking-associated DNA methylation (DNAm) changes in women. We measure whole blood DNAm (EPICv2) and self-reported smoking (three-category, pack-years, and years since cessation) via questionnaires in 6,005 Women’s Health Initiative Memory Study participants.
